Definition: properly, to go forth, i.e. (by implication) to be expelled, and (consequently) desolate; causatively, to lay waste; also (specifically), to quarrel
BiblicalUsage: Isaiah tells Hezekiah that the LORD formed long ago the laying waste of fenced cities into ruinous heaps, and the widow of Tekoah tells of her two sons striving together in the field until one strikes the other down.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the word cuts both ways: nations are laid waste and brothers quarrel, and the same word names the ruin of cities and the strife that begins in a field.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
